science.summary: Adds the surface emissions of trace gases and aerosols to the constituent surface fluxes $F_q$ that vertical diffusion will apply. It then checks that the surface moisture flux cannot empty the lowest layer: where a downward flux (dew or frost) would take the bottom-level humidity below its minimum, the downward flux is cut to what the layer can supply, and the latent heat of that change is taken from the sensible heat flux, so the surface energy flux is unchanged.

the backward-Euler step the implicit solver closes with Newton–Raphson iterations

science.summary: The trop_mam3 gas-phase chemistry and the MAM3 aerosol microphysics. The gas-phase mechanism carries SO₂, DMS, H₂O₂, H₂SO₄ and SOAG with prescribed oxidant fields; its stiff system is integrated by an explicit solver for the slow species and a backward-Euler (implicit) solver with Newton iterations for the rest. Soluble gases are washed out by precipitation, gases are dry-deposited at the surface, elevated emissions are added, and the aerosol step then exchanges mass between the gases and the aerosol modes: H₂SO₄ and SOAG condense, SO₂ is oxidised to sulfate in cloud water, new sulfate particles nucleate, and the Aitken mode coagulates into the accumulation mode.
science.title: Tropospheric chemistry (trop_mam3)

science.summary: Mixes heat, moisture, momentum and every constituent vertically by boundary-layer and free-atmosphere turbulence, and applies the surface fluxes received from the coupler as the lower boundary condition. The University of Washington scheme diagnoses the turbulent kinetic energy $e$ of each turbulent layer, including cloud-topped and elevated ones, and sets the eddy diffusivities from it; moist conserved variables ($s_l$, $q_t$) make the mixing consistent through cloud. The diffusion equation is solved implicitly. Turbulent mountain stress adds a form drag from unresolved orography at the surface.
science.title: Turbulent vertical diffusion (UW moist turbulence)

science.configuration: Only the orographic source is on (`use_gw_oro`); no spectrum of non-orographic waves (`pgwv = 0`), no frontal or convective sources. The efficiency $\varepsilon$ is `effgw_oro` = 0.125.

equations.caption: the launched stress, from the wind $U_0$, buoyancy frequency $N_0$ and density $\rho_0$ averaged over the depth of the obstacle, with horizontal wavenumber $k$ and critical Froude number $F_c$
the stress profile, limited by saturation as the wave propagates up
the drag on the wind component $U > 0$ along the launch direction, where the stress $\tau \ge 0$ decreases upward

references.citation: McFarlane, N. A. (1987). The effect of orographically excited gravity wave drag on the general circulation of the lower stratosphere and troposphere. Journal of the Atmospheric Sciences, 44(14), 1775–1800.
Neale, R. B., and Coauthors (2012). Description of the NCAR Community Atmosphere Model (CAM 5.0). NCAR Technical Note NCAR/TN-486+STR.

science.summary: Unresolved mountains launch stationary gravity waves that carry momentum upward and deposit it where they break, decelerating the flow aloft. Following McFarlane (1987), the launched stress depends on the low-level wind, stability and density and on the subgrid standard deviation of the orography $\sigma_h$. Going up, the stress is limited by the saturation stress, which shrinks where the wind weakens or the air thins; the stress lost between two levels decelerates the wind there, and the kinetic energy removed heats the air.
science.title: Orographic gravity wave drag

references.citation: Williamson, D. L. (2002). Time-split versus process-split coupling of parameterizations and dynamical core. Monthly Weather Review, 130(8), 2024–2041.

science.summary: Hands the physics tendencies to the spectral-element grid. The physics columns are the unique GLL points of the SE elements, so the mapping is a copy followed by an exchange along element edges. The temperature and wind tendencies are kept as forcing terms $F_T$, $F_{\mathbf{u}}$ that the dynamics applies during its steps; the tracer changes are applied at once, and the surface pressure changes by the mass of the water vapour the physics added or removed.
science.title: Physics–dynamics coupling, physics to dynamics

science.configuration:
`ne16np4` (13,826 columns, about 2° spacing), 30 levels; three 600 s dynamics steps per 1800 s physics step with the 5-stage, third-order Kinnmark–Gray Runge–Kutta (`tstep_type = 5`); vertical remap every three steps (`rsplit = 3`); hyperviscosity $
u = 7	imes10^{15}\ \mathrm{m^4\,s^{-1}}$ ($
u_{	ext{div}} = 1.55	imes10^{16}\ \mathrm{m^4\,s^{-1}}$), sponge $
u_{	ext{top}} = 2.5	imes10^{5}\ \mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}$; the optimization-based limiter (`se_limiter_option = 8`).

thermodynamics
mass, for the pressure thickness of a layer
each tracer $q$; with vertically Lagrangian levels $\dot\eta = 0$ during the dynamics steps and the remap does the vertical transport

CAM-SE: A scalable spectral element dynamical core for the Community Atmosphere Model. International Journal of High Performance Computing Applications, 26(1), 74–89.
Taylor, M. A., & Fournier, A. (2010). A compatible and conservative spectral element method on unstructured grids. Journal of Computational Physics, 229(17), 5879–5895.

Lin, S.-J. (2004). A "vertically Lagrangian" finite-volume dynamical core for global models. Monthly Weather Review, 132(10), 2293–2307.

science.summary: Solves the hydrostatic primitive equations on the cubed sphere with a continuous Galerkin spectral-element method: each of the 6 × 16 × 16 elements carries a 4 × 4 grid of Gauss–Lobatto–Legendre points, and neighbouring elements are joined by direct stiffness summation. Its spatial discretization conserves mass and energy. Fourth-order hyperviscosity removes grid-scale noise and a second-order sponge damps the top layers. Levels move with the flow (vertically Lagrangian) and are remapped to the hybrid levels; tracers are advected with a limiter that keeps them within their local bounds and conserves their mass.
science.title: Spectral-element dynamical core (CAM-SE)

science.summary: The dynamical core does not conserve total energy exactly. It also records the initial temperature and water, from which the step's dynamical-core tendency `DTCORE` is diagnosed.

science.summary: Represents precipitating cumulus towers too small for the grid. The Zhang–McFarlane scheme builds an ensemble of entraining updraft plumes and their downdrafts from the level of maximum moist static energy in the boundary layer. It triggers when the convective available potential energy (CAPE) of a dilute, entraining parcel exceeds a threshold, and its closure sets the cloud-base mass flux so that CAPE is consumed over a fixed time scale. The plumes transport heat, moisture and cloud water, condense and rain, evaporate precipitation below cloud, and transport momentum through convective pressure gradients.
science.title: Deep convection (Zhang–McFarlane)

equations.caption: the cloud-base mass flux: the upward flux of a Gaussian distribution of vertical velocities with variance from the boundary-layer mean TKE, counting only those faster than the critical velocity $w_c$ that overcomes the inhibition; $\rho_0$ is the density at the boundary-layer top and $b$ a buoyancy-efficiency constant
the plume, with entrainment and detrainment from buoyancy sorting

references.citation: Park, S., & Bretherton, C. S. (2009). The University of Washington shallow convection and moist turbulence schemes and their impact on climate simulations with the Community Atmosphere Model. Journal of Climate, 22(12), 3449–3469.

Bretherton, C. S., McCaa, J. R., & Grenier, H. (2004). A new parameterization for shallow cumulus convection and its application to marine subtropical cloud-topped boundary layers. Part I: Description and 1D results. Monthly Weather Review, 132(4), 864–882.

science.summary: Represents non-precipitating and weakly precipitating cumulus such as trade-wind clouds. The UW scheme launches a single entraining-detraining plume from the top of the boundary layer. Its cloud-base mass flux depends on the convective inhibition (CIN) and the boundary layer's turbulent kinetic energy: only the fraction of updrafts whose vertical velocity can overcome the CIN rises. Lateral mixing is determined by buoyancy sorting of the mixtures of cloudy and environmental air; condensate is detrained and precipitation forms above a threshold.
science.title: Shallow convection (University of Washington)

science.summary: Stratiform (large-scale) clouds and precipitation. The Park macrophysics computes the liquid and ice stratus fractions, from the relative humidity with a triangular distribution of subgrid humidity for liquid, and the condensation and evaporation that keep the cloud consistent with them; it also takes in the condensate detrained by convection. Aerosol activation then gives the droplet and ice crystal number sources, and the Morrison–Gettelman microphysics, a two-moment bulk scheme, predicts the mass and number of cloud liquid and ice and diagnoses rain and snow: autoconversion, accretion, freezing and melting, the Bergeron–Findeisen process, sedimentation and the evaporation of precipitation.
science.title: Cloud macrophysics and microphysics

science.summary: Solar (shortwave) and terrestrial (longwave) radiative transfer through gases, clouds and aerosols, giving the radiative heating rates and the surface fluxes. RRTMG is a correlated-$k$ model: 14 shortwave and 16 longwave bands, each integrated over its absorption coefficients by a small number of quadrature points. Subgrid cloud variability is sampled by McICA, which draws one random cloud profile per quadrature point consistent with the cloud fraction and its vertical overlap. Optical properties come from the prognostic water vapour and the MAM3 aerosol, prescribed ozone and fixed greenhouse gases.

cam_run1.cloud_macro_microphysics.name: cldfrc_premit
cam_run1.cloud_macro_microphysics.notes: Top of the mid-level RH ramp; dual copy as rhminl.

cam_run1.cloud_macro_microphysics.name: cldfrc_rhminh
cam_run1.cloud_macro_microphysics.notes: Minimum RH for high stable clouds; dual copy as rhminl.

cam_run1.cloud_macro_microphysics.name: cldfrc_rhminl
cam_run1.cloud_macro_microphysics.notes: Minimum RH for low stratus.  Initialization copies the value into cldwat2m_macro's rhminl_const, and the CAM5 macrophysics reads that shadow; both copies are written together.

cam_run1.cloud_macro_microphysics.name: cldfrc_rhminl_adj_land
cam_run1.cloud_macro_microphysics.notes: Snow-free-land adjustment to rhminl; dual copy as rhminl.

cam_run1.deep_convection.name: zmconv_c0_lnd
cam_run1.deep_convection.notes: Deep-convection autoconversion over land.  The namelist value passes by value from zm_conv_intr into zm_convi, which stores it in zm_conv's own module variable; only that copy is read afterwards.

cam_run1.deep_convection.name: zmconv_ke
cam_run1.deep_convection.notes: Evaporation efficiency of precipitation in ZM deep convection.

cam_run1.shallow_convection.name: cldfrc_sh1
cam_run1.shallow_convection.notes: Shallow-convective cloud-fraction coefficient.  Under CAM5 the surviving cldfrc output is concld, which sh1/sh2/dp1/dp2 control.

cam_run1.shallow_convection.name: uwshcu_rpen
cam_run1.shallow_convection.notes: Penetrative-entrainment efficiency of UW shallow convection.

cam_run1.label: Physics before surface coupling
cam_run1.summary: The parameterizations computed from the state the dynamics produced: the energy fixer, convection, clouds, aerosol wet removal and radiation. It ends by computing the fields the atmosphere sends to the surface: the bottom-level state, precipitation and downward radiation.

cam_run2.label: Physics after surface coupling
cam_run2.summary: The parameterizations that use the surface fluxes just received from the coupler: emissions, chemistry, turbulent vertical diffusion, dry deposition and gravity wave drag. It ends by handing the physics tendencies to the dynamical core.

cam_run3.label: Dynamics
cam_run3.summary: The spectral-element dynamical core advances the resolved flow, mass and tracers over one physics step: three 600 s dynamics steps.

clock.label: Clock
clock.summary: The model clock advances by one 1800 s step.

coupling.label: Surface coupling
coupling.summary: The atmosphere's exchange with the rest of CESM through the coupler. At the start of the step the fields from land (CLM), sea ice (CICE), the data ocean (DOCN) and runoff are copied into CAM; at the end, the atmosphere's surface state is handed back.
